findings: The matching official 85.9% measures recipients by place/provision type. Footnote 1 distinguishes exclusive cash-benefit recipients from combination-benefit recipients; no work-hour or task denominator appears. A literal work-volume claim is not established by that table.

The numerical match and earlier recipient wording make a recipient-to-work compression plausible, but do not identify the exact source used for the Septemberletter. The author gives no year, release, table or footnote. Matching one number cannot exclude another source or an informal caseload description.

The author’s qualification often unremunerated matters: it does not literally claim every part of the 86% is unpaid. Civil society is undefined and can include organisations providing paid services. Professional ambulatory care in the home group therefore cannot simply be subtracted to obtain a correct unpaid-work share.

A large home-care recipient population does support the general importance of family-care participation, even though it does not quantify the national share of work. Family help can also accompany institutional care; home recipients need differing amounts of care.

The record correctly leaves the numerical correction’s direction null. Neither a smaller work share nor a policy implication has been proved. Potential imprecision remains minor under the plausible shorthand interpretation.
The exact PNOG draft remains unauthenticated for this open letter. This is an additional scope/version limitation, not proof that the statistical source attribution is false.
limits: This review confirms the identified table’s measure and arithmetic, not the nonexistence of all possible Destatis work-share estimates. No replacement work share, intent, author response, policy efficacy or lawful-participation conclusion inferred.
